results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 39 aligned units match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in the spec's order; the three callouts match no spec paragraph. The outline of Stripe and Adyen ¶2 adds 'normalise vocabulary', an addition inside the unit and not a different idea.

results.draft_locus: Where a Provider Can Stand in the Chain ¶3
results.quote: The section reduces to the question I would put to any provider before any other: **which legal entity is the acquirer for these sellers, in this country?**
results.finding: The unit holds two controlling ideas: the platform is a layer that stays out of the money, and the first question for any provider is who the acquirer is. The second is a conclusion of the whole section (the draft says so: 'The section reduces to'), not of the platform paragraph. The spec's own controlling idea for p26 is double, joined by a 'so' that does not follow; its changelog records the unacted flow-rubric note 'give the acquirer-of-record question its own paragraph'. Splitting needs a changed unit structure. (The other marked unit, Timeline ¶4, is ruled one idea: its topic sentence 'Step three is a record and step four is the first movement of money' states a single record-then-money contrast, the section's own claim.)

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: parties and variants to S1; scene, timeline and walkthrough to S2 and S3; provider positions and the Stripe and Adyen comparison to S4; failures to S3. The requirements table (Timeline ¶7) ties to S3 (statuses are delayed reports).

Each quotation, table and figure is introduced or followed by a sentence saying what it shows, and each figure has a caption that does. Two points are recorded under flow_is_followable, not here: the failure table lacks the spec's capture row, and Figure 1's four notes differ from the paragraph's four facts.

results.draft_locus: The Timeline: A Message, a Record, Then Money ¶1
results.quote: Three different things move in a card payment, and they move in a fixed order: **a message, then a record, then money**.
results.finding: The declared transition carries over the parties and what each holds and risks, and introduces the order in which they act. The section opens on a new claim; nothing at the boundary (the figure caption before it, or this sentence) picks up the parties, who reappear only in the Mastercard quotation and the 'Who acts' column.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Larkfield: One Word for Four Facts ¶2
results.quote: A phone showing one green tick beside four pinned notes labeled Approved, Claimed, Settled and Paid out, each with its own clock.
results.finding: Both flow readers went back to compare two lists of 'four facts': Femke's questions are who approved, has money moved, when the studio receives it, until when it can be taken back; the figure's four notes are Approved, Claimed, Settled, Paid out (a claim, and no take-back). The figure and its caption present a different four from the paragraph they illustrate.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 2 (flow reader A reported the same point as item 8)

results.draft_locus: The Parties: Four in the Model, More in Practice ¶5
results.quote: The rest of the table is a generalization: **contracts and local law can move any cell**.
results.finding: 'The table' has not appeared yet: the sentence points forward to the money-and-risk table while the table the reader has just read is the names table above. Both readers looked upward first. The same sentence carries the label AC-3 requires, so the pointer should be unambiguous ('the table below').
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 5 (flow reader A reported the same point as item 4)

results.draft_locus: The Parties: Four in the Model, More in Practice ¶5
results.quote: Between settlement and payout, a merchant's money is as safe as its acquirer or provider.
results.finding: 'Settlement' is used as a known point in time and as money received ('receives the settlement', 'between settlement and payout' in the names table of ¶4, this sentence, the money-and-risk table) a section before the timeline defines it. It is on the spec's does_not_know list and AC-2 requires one plain clause before use; the introduction describes the step without attaching the word. Both readers were 'working from a guess' until the next section. A one-clause gloss at first use fits the length budget (6,203 of 6,500 words); the spec's order need not change, though its flow rubric note (move p12 after the timeline) and both readers point the same way. 'Payout' is judged given by the introduction's 'the payment provider pays the merchant'.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, item 3, and flow reader B, item 4

results.draft_locus: The Parties: Four in the Model, More in Practice ¶3
results.quote: A Member that signs a Merchant or Payment Facilitator
results.finding: 'Payment Facilitator', a term AC-2 lists, first appears inside the Visa quotation two paragraphs before the names table defines it, with no gloss.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, item 2, and flow reader B, item 3

results.draft_locus: The Parties: Four in the Model, More in Practice ¶3

results.finding: 'Interchange' in the rulebook sense is used here and glossed only in Timeline ¶4 ('in the rulebook "Interchange" means this exchange of records, not the fee'). results.draft_locus: When It Goes Wrong: Each Step Fails in Its Own Way ¶1
results.quote: Larkfield's incidents ([[meet-larkfield]]) fall along the timeline, one per hand-off between two parties.
results.finding: The paragraph says each step fails in its own way and announces one incident per hand-off, but the table has no row for capture or clearing, merges 'Settlement and after', and ends with a row that is neither a step nor a hand-off. Both readers checked the table against the six steps and they did not line up. The spec's table for p34 has a capture row (the approval expires before the claim) and a 'clearing and settlement' row; the draft dropped the first and renamed the second.

results.draft_locus: In Practice at Larkfield: Mila's €120, Party by Party ¶2
results.quote: €117.47 in the studio's bank account; €2.53 in Larkfield's balance at Adyen
results.finding: One reader (B, item 17) stopped because the money does not add up: the settlement row says less than €120 reaches the acquirer ('less interchange'), yet payout and fee total the full €120, and who bears the interchange and the provider's cost is not said. A clause pointing to payment-economics would close it without the breakdown the spec excludes.

results.draft_locus: The Timeline: A Message, a Record, Then Money ¶5
results.quote: Step five belongs to the provider, and here the providers' own words can mislead, because both use "settlement" for their release of funds to the merchant.
results.finding: One reader (B, item 8) read the paragraph twice: the Stripe quotation is about what 'T' counts from and does not show Stripe using 'settlement' for a payout, so the evidence does not match the opening claim for Stripe. The spec's point for that quotation is that Stripe's 'settlement timing' counts from capture; the draft omits the phrase that carries it.

results.draft_locus: The Timeline: A Message, a Record, Then Money ¶3
results.quote: The promise also expires: Visa's rules (edition of 24 October 2026) give an acquirer at most 10 calendar days to process an ordinary online payment that the customer started.
results.finding: One reader (B, item 6) had to re-read: the paragraph is about the issuer's promise and the merchant's capture, and the sentence switches to an acquirer 'processing' without saying that the claim must be presented within 10 days of the approval.

results.quote: every step of a payment has an owner, and the provider owns only one, the payout
results.finding: One reader (A, item 13) had to reconcile this with the worked example, where Adyen also captures, presents the clearing record and receives the settlement; the sentence does not say that it does those as acquirer. A short qualification fixes it without changing the claim.
The introduction opens on a dated, puzzling scenario (where is the €120 at 19:43?), states the thesis in its second paragraph and gives a roadmap; none of the five weak patterns.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic, sorts its points by how settled they are and ends on a synthesis, a course of action and the hand-off; none of the weak patterns.

The synthesis bullet says what no single section says ('The parties, the timeline and the provider's position are one fact seen three ways: every step of a payment has an owner') and gives the consequence ('I would store it that way: which promise, from whom, open until when'; ask for the acquirer of record first).

The closing paragraph returns to the opening minute ('At 19:43 on 9 March the screen said the payment had succeeded and the €120 had not moved') and says what the reader can now state about it, as callback.how asks.

From the introduction alone the reader predicted all seven body sections in the roadmap's order, the three kinds of evidence (the dated worked example, provider documentation with access dates, network facts) and the plain, corrective tone. The reader could not tell where the 'four facts' are treated or whether the ending calls back; neither is a roadmap promise.

The probe answer matches the expected answer: the issuer alone has decided and holds the €60, reserved on the customer's account; the network carried and the provider relayed; no money has moved (capture, if automatic, is an instruction); clearing, settlement between the banks and the payout have not happened; the dispute window stays open for about 120 days.

Statements about Stripe's and Adyen's roles carry a source and a date or access date (the acquirer disclosure, license pages, annual report, payout pages; the 2019 and 2020 sources carry an evidence age), or are marked 'Not public' or as the author's inference (acquirer of record for Mila's payment; the INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED block). The money-and-risk table is labeled: 'The rest of the table is a generalization: contracts and local law can move any cell'. The label's ambiguous pointer is recorded under flow_is_followable.
